eta.tooltip: Controls the scale of the parallel guidance vector. Default CFG behavior at a setting of 1.

momentum.tooltip: Controls a running average of guidance during diffusion, disabled at a setting of 0.

norm_threshold.tooltip: Normalize guidance vector to this value, normalization disable at a setting of 0.

blend_mode.tooltip: Initial blend mode, applied against the layers below. On the bottom layer over the default transparent background, non-normal modes produce transparency.

height.tooltip: Initial display height. 0 keeps the image's native height.

layers.tooltip: Layer stack to append to. Leave unconnected to start a new stack.

mask.tooltip: Transparency mask for this layer. Masked areas (value 1) become transparent, multiplying with any alpha channel the image already carries.

name.tooltip: Layer name shown in the compositor editor.

width.tooltip: Initial display width. 0 keeps the image's native width.

x.tooltip: Initial horizontal placement on the canvas.

y.tooltip: Initial vertical placement on the canvas.

z_index.tooltip: Stacking override. Layers are stable-sorted by z_index; equal values keep their list order.

image.tooltip: Layer content at its native size. A batch expands to consecutive layers.

AddTextPrefix.description: Add a prefix to all texts.
AddTextPrefix.name: AddTextPrefix

AddTextSuffix.description: Add a suffix to all texts.
AddTextSuffix.name: AddTextSuffix

AdjustBrightness.description: Adjust the brightness of an image.

factor.tooltip: Brightness factor. 1.0 = no change, <1.0 = darker, >1.0 = brighter.

images.tooltip: Image to process.

AdjustBrightness.name: AdjustBrightness

AdjustContrast.description: Adjust the contrast of an image.

factor.tooltip: Contrast factor. 1.0 = no change, <1.0 = less contrast, >1.0 = more contrast.

images.tooltip: Image to process.

AdjustContrast.name: AdjustContrast

ApplyTextureToMesh.description: Attaches baked texture IMAGEs to a mesh's UV layout for SaveGLB. Feed the SAME mesh you baked
ApplyTextureToMesh.name: ApplyTextureToMesh

AudioAdjustVolume.description: Adjust the volume of the audio by a specified amount in decibels (dB).

volume.tooltip: Volume adjustment in decibels (dB). 0 = no change, +6 = double, -6 = half, etc

AudioAdjustVolume.name: AudioAdjustVolume

AudioConcat.description: Concatenates the audio1 to audio2 in the specified direction.

direction.tooltip: Whether to append audio2 after or before audio1.

AudioConcat.name: AudioConcat

AudioMerge.description: Combine two audio tracks by overlaying their waveforms.

merge_method.tooltip: The method used to combine the audio waveforms.

AudioMerge.name: AudioMerge

BakeAmbientOcclusion.description: Bakes an ambient-occlusion map from a high-poly mesh into a low-poly's UV layout (white = open, dark = crevices). Feed the UV-unwrapped low_poly and the high_poly it was decimated from. Outputs a grayscale image for Apply Texture To Mesh's occlusion input (packed into the ORM map / occlusionTexture).

bias.tooltip: Ray origin lift off the surface, as a fraction of the bounding box diagonal. Raise if even surfaces show dark blotches/holes.

max_distance.tooltip: Ray length, as a fraction of the bounding box diagonal. Smaller = tighter, more local occlusion.

samples.tooltip: Rays per texel. More = smoother, slower. Raise if grainy.

BakeAmbientOcclusion.name: BakeAmbientOcclusion

BakeNormalMapFromMesh.description: Bakes a tangent-space normal map (glTF/OpenGL +Y) from a high-poly mesh into a low-poly's UV layout, capturing detail lost during decimation. Feed the UV-unwrapped low_poly and the high_poly it was decimated from. Outputs an image for Apply Texture To Mesh's normal_map input.

cage_distance.tooltip: Surface search band, as a fraction of the bounding box diagonal. Raise for wrong/missing patches under heavy decimation; lower if it grabs across gaps.

ignore_backfaces.tooltip: Skip high-poly surfaces facing away from the texel, so crevices/enclosed spaces don't grab the opposite wall. Disable only if the high-poly winding is inconsistent.

BakeNormalMapFromMesh.name: BakeNormalMapFromMesh

BakeTextureFromVoxel.description: Bakes PBR textures onto the mesh's existing UV layout (trilinear-sample the sparse voxel volume). Does NOT unwrap — connect a UV unwrap node upstream. Outputs base_color + metallic/roughness grayscale IMAGEs (black if no PBR); feed them to ApplyTextureToMesh (SAME mesh) for SaveGLB.

reference_mesh.tooltip: Optional dense pre-decimation mesh; back-projects each texel onto its true surface before sampling, removing faceted baking on coarse meshes.

BakeTextureFromVoxel.name: BakeTextureFromVoxel

BeebleSwitchXImageEdit.description: Edit a single image with Beeble SwitchX. Switches anything in the scene (background, lighting, costume) while preserving the original subject's pixels. Provide a reference image and/or text prompt to describe the new look. Max ~2.77MP.

reference_image.tooltip: Reference image whose look (background, lighting, costume) the result should adopt. At least one of 'reference_image' or 'prompt' is required.

alpha_mode.tooltip: Controls how SwitchX decides what to keep vs. regenerate. 'auto' isolates the main subject automatically. 'fill' regenerates the entire frame while preserving geometry. 'select' propagates a first-frame keyframe across the clip. 'custom' uses a per-frame alpha matte you provide.

prompt.tooltip: Text description of the desired output (max 2000 chars). At least one of 'prompt' or 'reference_image' is required.

seed.tooltip: Seed controls whether the node should re-run; results are non-deterministic regardless of seed.

BeebleSwitchXImageEdit.name: BeebleSwitchXImageEdit

BeebleSwitchXVideoEdit.description: Edit a video with Beeble SwitchX. Switches anything in the scene (background, lighting, costume) while preserving the original subject's pixels and motion. Provide a reference image and/or text prompt to describe the new look. Max 240 frames, max ~2.77MP per frame.

reference_image.tooltip: Reference image whose look (background, lighting, costume) the result should adopt. At least one of 'reference_image' or 'prompt' is required.

alpha_keyframe.tooltip: First-frame keyframe mask. Beeble propagates this across the video.

alpha_mask.tooltip: Per-frame grayscale mask covering the entire video. Must have the same frame count as the source. Connect a MASK output from SAM3_TrackToMask or similar.

alpha_mode.tooltip: Controls how SwitchX decides what to keep vs. regenerate. 'auto' isolates the main subject automatically. 'fill' regenerates the entire frame while preserving geometry. 'select' propagates a first-frame keyframe across the clip. 'custom' uses a per-frame alpha matte you provide.

prompt.tooltip: Text description of the desired output (max 2000 chars). At least one of 'prompt' or 'reference_image' is required.

seed.tooltip: Seed controls whether the node should re-run; results are non-deterministic regardless of seed.

BeebleSwitchXVideoEdit.name: BeebleSwitchXVideoEdit

BerniniConditioning.description: Conditioning node for Bernini in-context video/image conditioning. It can be used for the following tasks: t2v (text-to-video), v2v (video-to-video), rv2v (reference-guided video editing), r2v (reference-to-video), ads2v (insert image/video into video).Reference images injected as in-context tokens (r2v, rv2v) are encoded independently at their own native aspect ratio (long edge capped at ref_max_size)

ref_max_size.tooltip: Max size for the long edge of reference_video and reference_images. Resized with preserved aspect ratio and snapped to 16px.

reference_image.tooltip: Reference image injected as an in-context token (r2v, rv2v).

reference_video.tooltip: Video to insert into the source video (ads2v).

source_video.tooltip: Source video to edit or restyle (v2v, rv2v). Resized to width/height and trimmed to length.

BerniniConditioning.name: BerniniConditioning

BlockSparseAttention.description: Applies block-sparse attention to eligible model attention layers, reducing compute for long sequences. The speed gain grows with sequence length since short sequences are usually faster dense. Outside the start/end_percent, dense_blocks and under min_tokens, the model uses the dense model attention backend. Use the node Model Attention Backend to select that fallback.

dense_blocks.tooltip: Transformer blocks that always run dense, e.g. '0, 1, 47-49'.

end_percent.tooltip: Percentage point when sparse attention ends. After this point, attention returns to dense.

extra_tokens.tooltip: Extra top-scoring tokens each query block attends beyond its selected blocks. Closer to dense for more attention time; 256 recommended, 0 disables. Ignored for VSA.

min_tokens.tooltip: Sequences shorter than this stay dense.

model.tooltip: The model to patch.

tau.tooltip: Threshold in score-distribution sigmas. Higher is sparser: 1.0 keeps ~16% of key blocks exact, 1.5 ~7%, 2.0 ~2.7%.

keep_percent.tooltip: Percent of key blocks each query block keeps exactly (sinks and the diagonal ride on top). The selection SLA-style LoRAs are distilled against; without such a LoRA higher is closer to dense.
Percent of video cubes each query cube keeps; FastH3-VSA checkpoints are trained at 10. Uses the model's to_gate_compress layers for the coarse branch when present.

selection.tooltip: Method used to choose key blocks for full token-level attention. sol-attn: Sparsifying Online Attention uses a training-free adaptive threshold for each attention head and query block. sla: Sparse-Linear Attention keeps a fixed percentage of the highest-scoring key blocks; use only with model weights trained for this pattern. vsa: Video Sparse Attention (FastVideo) uses 3D video-cube tiling and a learned coarse attention branch; requires FastH3 model weights.

sink_conditioning.tooltip: MiniMax-H3 only. exact_kv: every query attends the packed text/audio/reference rows exactly (~3% cost). exact_kv_and_rows: additionally runs the target-audio query rows dense (keeps generated audio intact).

start_percent.tooltip: Percentage point when sparse attention begins. Before this point, attention stays dense.

verbose.tooltip: Logs whether each attention shape used sparse attention or why it stayed dense.

BlockSparseAttention.name: BlockSparseAttention

BriaAddObject.description: Insert an object described in plain text into an image using Bria. Bria re-renders the whole frame at about 1 megapixel, so the result is not pixel-aligned with the input.

instruction.tooltip: What to add and where, such as 'Place a red vase with flowers on the table'.

seed.tooltip: Bria takes no seed here and re-imagines the edit on each call, so repeated runs can differ. The value is never sent: it only changes this node's cache key, so that an otherwise identical graph runs the edit again instead of returning the cached result.

BriaAddObject.name: BriaAddObject

BriaEraseByText.description: Remove an object named in plain text from an image using Bria. Bria re-renders the whole frame at about 1 megapixel, so the result is not pixel-aligned with the input.

object_name.tooltip: Name of the object to remove, such as 'the lamp'. Several objects can be named at once, such as 'the phone and the pencils'. Naming something that is not in the picture still returns, and bills, a re-rendered image.

BriaEraseByText.name: BriaEraseByText

BriaEraseForeground.description: Remove the foreground of an image with Bria and generate a background in its place. Everything Bria reads as foreground goes, not only people. The untouched pixels are preserved, but the output is re-rendered at a standard size close to 1 megapixel.
BriaEraseForeground.name: BriaEraseForeground

BriaEraser.description: Remove objects or areas outlined by a mask from an image using Bria.

mask.tooltip: White areas are erased, black areas are preserved. The mask is binarized before sending, so partially painted areas count as white. Must have the same aspect ratio as the image.

mask_type.tooltip: manual for hand-drawn or brush masks, automatic for masks produced by segmentation models such as SAM.

BriaEraser.name: BriaEraser

BriaExpandImage.description: Expand an image beyond its borders with generated content using Bria.

ratio_height.tooltip: Height side of the target ratio: 21 and 9 give 21:9. Bria only accepts width/height between 0.5 and 3.0, so anything taller than 1:2 needs the manual mode.

ratio_width.tooltip: Width side of the target ratio: 21 and 9 give 21:9.

image_height.tooltip: Height of the original image inside the canvas.

image_width.tooltip: Width of the original image inside the canvas.

image_x.tooltip: X position of the image's top-left corner inside the canvas; may fall outside the canvas, cropping the image.

image_y.tooltip: Y position of the image's top-left corner inside the canvas; may fall outside the canvas, cropping the image.

expand_mode.tooltip: Target shape of the expanded image: a preset aspect ratio, a custom ratio, or manual placement of the original image on a canvas. Manual is the only mode that can reach a canvas taller than 1:2.

prompt.tooltip: Optional description of the expanded scene; when empty, Bria generates one from the image.

BriaExpandImage.name: BriaExpandImage

BriaGenFill.description: Generate objects or scenery inside a masked region of an image using Bria.

mask.tooltip: White areas are filled with generated content, black areas are preserved. The mask is binarized before sending, so partially painted areas count as white. Must have the same aspect ratio as the image.

prompt.tooltip: Description of what to generate inside the masked region.

refine_prompt.tooltip: Automatically adjust the prompt for better results; disable to use the prompt exactly as written.

BriaGenFill.name: BriaGenFill

BriaImageEditNode.description: Edit images using Bria latest model

mask.tooltip: If omitted, the edit applies to the entire image.

guidance_scale.tooltip: Higher value makes the image follow the prompt more closely.

prompt.tooltip: Instruction to edit image

structured_prompt.tooltip: A string containing the structured edit prompt in JSON format. Use this instead of usual prompt for precise, programmatic control.

BriaImageEditNode.name: BriaImageEditNode

BriaIncreaseResolution.description: Upscale an image by 2x or 4x using Bria, preserving the original content.

auto_downscale.tooltip: Automatically lower the multiplier, and downscale the input image if that is still not enough, when the output would exceed the limit.

desired_increase.tooltip: Resolution multiplier. The output must fit within 8192 pixels on each side.

BriaIncreaseResolution.name: BriaIncreaseResolution

BriaRelight.description: Change the lighting atmosphere and direction of an image using Bria. Bria re-renders the whole frame at about 1 megapixel, so the result is not pixel-aligned with the input.

light_direction.tooltip: Where the light comes from. Hard-light atmospheres such as midday, spotlight on subject and harsh studio lighting react to it the most.

BriaRelight.name: BriaRelight

BriaRemoveImageBackground.description: Remove the background from an image using Bria RMBG 2.0.

seed.tooltip: Seed controls whether the node should re-run; results are non-deterministic regardless of seed.

BriaRemoveImageBackground.name: BriaRemoveImageBackground

BriaRemoveVideoBackground.description: Remove the background from a video using Bria.

background_color.tooltip: Background color for the output video.

seed.tooltip: Seed controls whether the node should re-run; results are non-deterministic regardless of seed.

BriaRemoveVideoBackground.name: BriaRemoveVideoBackground

BriaReplaceImageBackground.description: Replace the background of an image with Bria, described by a prompt or guided by reference images. The subject's pixels are preserved; the background is generated around them.

mode.tooltip: high_control follows the prompt most closely, base is a balanced default and fast trades detail for speed.

prompt.tooltip: Description of the new background. A hex color code such as #FF5733 produces a solid color background.

refine_prompt.tooltip: Rewrite the prompt for better results, which also translates non-English prompts. Turn it off to send the prompt exactly as written.

enhance_ref_images.tooltip: Extra processing of the reference images for better results.

ref_images.tooltip: 1-10 images guiding the new background; they do not need to share a size. Every reference changes the result, so a few consistent ones beat many conflicting ones. A batched input counts once per image.

background.tooltip: Describe the new background with a prompt, or guide it with reference images.

original_quality.tooltip: Return the input's exact pixel size instead of scaling the result to about 1 megapixel. A large input then returns a large image.

seed.tooltip: The same seed usually returns the same background; the automatic prompt refinement can still vary it.

BriaReplaceImageBackground.name: BriaReplaceImageBackground

BriaReplaceObject.description: Swap an object in an image for another one described in plain text using Bria. Bria re-renders the whole frame at about 1 megapixel, so the result is not pixel-aligned with the input.

instruction.tooltip: What to replace with what, such as 'Replace the red apple with a green pear'.

seed.tooltip: Bria takes no seed here and re-imagines the edit on each call, so repeated runs can differ. The value is never sent: it only changes this node's cache key, so that an otherwise identical graph runs the edit again instead of returning the cached result.

BriaReplaceObject.name: BriaReplaceObject

BriaReseason.description: Move an image to another season with Bria. The whole scene is re-rendered, so scenery can change beyond the season itself. Bria re-renders the whole frame at about 1 megapixel, so the result is not pixel-aligned with the input.
BriaReseason.name: BriaReseason

BriaRestorePhoto.description: Repair an old or damaged photograph with Bria: grain, scratches and blur go, and age-related color casts are neutralized. Card mounts and studio borders may be cropped away and faces are re-drawn. Bria re-renders the whole frame at about 1 megapixel, so the result is not pixel-aligned with the input. Use Bria Increase Resolution to enlarge instead.
BriaRestorePhoto.name: BriaRestorePhoto

BriaTransparentVideoBackground.description: Remove the background from a video using Bria and return the cut-out frames plus an alpha mask. Connect both to a compositing node, or feed them to Save WEBM to write a transparent video.

seed.tooltip: Seed controls whether the node should re-run; results are non-deterministic regardless of seed.

BriaTransparentVideoBackground.name: BriaTransparentVideoBackground

BriaVideoEraser.description: Erase whatever a per-frame mask covers from a video with Bria and fill the gap in. The mask must be white on what should go and black elsewhere. Bria accepts clips of at most 5.1 seconds at 20 to 30 frames per second with even pixel dimensions; audio is kept by default. The returned clip can be a few frames shorter than the input.

mask.tooltip: One mask per frame of the video, white where the object to erase is. Provide either a mask or a mask video, not both.

mask_video.tooltip: An already encoded mask video with the same dimensions and frame count as the video. Provide either a mask or a mask video, not both.

video.tooltip: Clip to erase from.

BriaVideoEraser.name: BriaVideoEraser

BriaVideoGreenScreen.description: Replace a video's background with a solid chroma-key screen using Bria.

green_shade.tooltip: Solid chroma-key shade applied behind the foreground: broadcast_green (#00B140), chroma_green (#00FF00), or blue_screen (#0000FF).

seed.tooltip: Seed controls whether the node should re-run; results are non-deterministic regardless of seed.

BriaVideoGreenScreen.name: BriaVideoGreenScreen

BriaVideoReplaceBackground.description: Replace a video's background with a supplied image or video using Bria. The output keeps the foreground's resolution and frame rate; a background with a different aspect ratio is stretched to fit, so match it for undistorted results.

background_image.tooltip: Background image to composite behind the foreground. Provide either a background image or a background video, not both.

background_video.tooltip: Background video to composite behind the foreground. Provide either a background image or a background video, not both.

seed.tooltip: Seed controls whether the node should re-run; results are non-deterministic regardless of seed.

video.tooltip: Foreground video whose background is replaced.

BriaVideoReplaceBackground.name: BriaVideoReplaceBackground

BuildJsonPromptIdeogram.description: Build a JSON prompt for the Ideogram 4 model.

aesthetics.tooltip: Mandatory aesthetic keywords (e.g. moody, cinematic, desaturated).

background.tooltip: Mandatory description of the image background or environment.

color_palette.tooltip: Hex color codes that steer the image's dominant colors. Up to 16 entries.

element.tooltip: Prompt elements from the node Create Bounding Boxes.

high_level_description.tooltip: Optional description of the image in one or two sentences. Strongly recommended.

lighting.tooltip: Mandatory lighting description (e.g. golden hour, rim light, dramatic shadows).

medium.tooltip: Mandatory medium type (e.g. photograph, illustration, 3d_render, painting, graphic_design). When style = photo, set to photograph.

photo.tooltip: Camera or lens details for photographic outputs (e.g. 35mm, f/1.4, bokeh).

art_style.tooltip: Art style description (e.g. flat vector illustration, bold outlines).

BuildJsonPromptIdeogram.name: BuildJsonPromptIdeogram

BuildPoseFile.description: Build an animated GLB from pose data, or save a BVH mocap file.

camera_translation.tooltip: Bake pred_cam_t into the root's translation 'off' = bind position 'centered' = delta from frame 0 'absolute' = raw (Z is camera depth — usually meters away).

bone_smooth_window.tooltip: Gaussian smoothing window on per-bone rotation keyframes / keypoint tracks. 0 = off. 7-15 calms spins/jitter where upstream Smooth misses spikes.

bone_vis_color.tooltip: Per-bone vertex colors (unlit material). 'white' = none, 'rainbow_y' = head→toe jet.

bone_vis_radius_m.tooltip: Radius in m (sphere radius / octahedron half-width).

bone_vis.tooltip: Bone vis shape, rigidly skinned to each joint.

person_palette_falloff.tooltip: Per-person desaturation: each track gets (1 - falloff^k) pastel mix.

rainbow_tilt_x.tooltip: Rotate rainbow jet axis around X (right). Differentiates front/back.

rainbow_tilt_z.tooltip: Rotate rainbow jet axis around Z (forward). Differentiates left/right.

person_palette_falloff.tooltip: Per-person desaturation: each track gets (1 - falloff^k) pastel mix.

rainbow_tilt_x.tooltip: Rotate rainbow jet axis around X (right). Differentiates front/back.

rainbow_tilt_z.tooltip: Rotate rainbow jet axis around Z (forward). Differentiates left/right.

person_palette_falloff.tooltip: Per-person desaturation: each track gets (1 - falloff^k) pastel mix.

rainbow_tilt_x.tooltip: Rotate rainbow jet axis around X (right). Differentiates front/back.

rainbow_tilt_z.tooltip: Rotate rainbow jet axis around Z (forward). Differentiates left/right.

shader.tooltip: Bake per-vertex colors matching the Render node's shaders (COLOR_0 + KHR_materials_unlit). 'default' = no colors.

bone_vis_color.tooltip: Per-bone vertex colors (unlit material). 'white' = none, 'rainbow_y' = head→toe jet.

bone_vis_radius_m.tooltip: Radius in m (sphere radius / octahedron half-width).

bone_vis.tooltip: Bone vis shape, rigidly skinned to each joint. 'octahedrons' = Blender-style directional bones (joint → primary child).

face_marker_radius_m.tooltip: Face dot radius. 0 = auto = 0.3 x marker_radius_m.

face_style.tooltip: Face-contour landmarks sampled from pred_vertices at fixed head-mesh vertex IDs (needs canonical_colors on pose_data). 'full' = all ~30 points; 'eyes_mouth' = eyes + outer lips only.

include_hands.tooltip: Append 21+21 OpenPose hands (wrist + 5 fingers x 4 joints, base→tip) sourced from pred_keypoints_3d.

stick_radius_m.tooltip: Limb half-width in m. Auto-clamped to bone_length x 0.1.

face_style.tooltip: Face-contour landmarks sampled from pred_vertices (needs canonical_colors on pose_data). 'full' = all ~30 points; 'eyes_mouth' = eyes + outer lips only.

include_hands.tooltip: Append 21+21 hand keypoints + capsule sticks per track.

marker_radius_m.tooltip: Joint sphere radius. 0 = auto = stick_radius_m (flush cap).

material_roughness.tooltip: PBR roughness. SCAIL ref = 0.3. 1 = matte; 0 = chrome.

stick_radius_m.tooltip: Cylinder radius in m. Bones are open cylinders at constant radius; joint spheres (auto-sized to match) cap the open ends. SCAIL reference = 0.0215 m.

mesh_style.tooltip: 'body_mesh' = real Armature (127 bones, skinning, TRS keyframes, 72 face morphs; needs model). 'bones_only' = bone-shape primitives at each joint (preview armature). 'openpose' = OpenPose-18 3D skeleton from keypoints 'scail' = SCAIL 3D capsule rig (open cylinders capped flush by joint spheres).

units.tooltip: BVH OFFSET/position units. 'cm' is the mocap standard.

format.tooltip: Output format, both fed to Save 3D Model to write to disk. 'glb' = animated GLB (mesh / bones / openpose / scail). 'bvh' = BVH mocap clip (one skeleton; needs the model).

BuildPoseFile.name: BuildPoseFile

ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode.description: Generate video using Seedance 2.5 or 2.0 from a first frame image and optional last frame image.

first_frame.tooltip: First frame image for the video.

first_frame_asset_id.tooltip: Seedance asset_id to use as the first frame. Mutually exclusive with the first_frame image input.

last_frame.tooltip: Last frame image for the video.

last_frame_asset_id.tooltip: Seedance asset_id to use as the last frame. Mutually exclusive with the last_frame image input.

duration.tooltip: Duration of the output video in seconds (4-30).

generate_audio.tooltip: Enable audio generation for the output video.

output_format.tooltip: Container format of the output video.

prompt.tooltip: Text prompt for video generation. Put spoken lines in double quotes to steer the generated dialogue.

duration.tooltip: Duration of the output video in seconds (4-15).

generate_audio.tooltip: Enable audio generation for the output video.

prompt.tooltip: Text prompt for video generation.

ratio.tooltip: Aspect ratio of the output video.

duration.tooltip: Duration of the output video in seconds (4-15).

generate_audio.tooltip: Enable audio generation for the output video.

prompt.tooltip: Text prompt for video generation.

ratio.tooltip: Aspect ratio of the output video.

generate_audio.tooltip: Enable audio generation for the output video.

prompt.tooltip: Text prompt for video generation.

ratio.tooltip: Aspect ratio of the output video.

model.tooltip: Seedance 2.5 for the newest model, videos up to 30 seconds and mp4/mov output; Seedance 2.0 for maximum quality and 4k; Fast for speed optimization; Mini for the fastest, lowest-cost generation.

seed.tooltip: Seed controls whether the node should re-run; results are non-deterministic regardless of seed.

watermark.tooltip: Whether to add a watermark to the video.

ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode.name: ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode

ByteDance2ReferenceNode.description: Generate, edit, or extend video using Seedance 2.5 or 2.0 with reference images, videos, and audio. Supports multimodal reference, video editing, and video extension.

auto_downscale.tooltip: Automatically downscale reference videos that exceed the model's pixel budget for the selected resolution. Aspect ratio is preserved; videos already within limits are untouched.

auto_upscale.tooltip: Automatically upscale reference videos that are below the model's minimum pixel count for the selected resolution. Aspect ratio is preserved; videos already meeting the minimum are untouched. Note: upscaling a low-resolution source does not add real detail and may produce lower-quality generations.

duration.tooltip: Duration of the output video in seconds (4-30).

generate_audio.tooltip: Enable audio generation for the output video.

output_format.tooltip: Container format of the output video.

prompt.tooltip: Text prompt for video generation. Put spoken lines in double quotes to steer the generated dialogue.

ratio.tooltip: Aspect ratio of the output video.

video_editing.tooltip: Enable when the prompt edits a connected reference video, for example replacing an object in it. The output then keeps the source clip's own length and aspect ratio, and the duration and ratio widgets are ignored. Leave disabled to generate a new video, or to extend one to the duration you set.

ByteDance2ReferenceNodeV2.description: Generate, edit, or extend video using Seedance 2.5 or 2.0 with reference images, videos, and audio. Supports multimodal reference, video editing, and video extension.

auto_downscale.tooltip: Automatically downscale reference videos that exceed the model's pixel budget for the selected resolution. Aspect ratio is preserved; videos already within limits are untouched.

auto_upscale.tooltip: Automatically upscale reference videos that are below the model's minimum pixel count for the selected resolution. Aspect ratio is preserved; videos already meeting the minimum are untouched. Note: upscaling a low-resolution source does not add real detail and may produce lower-quality generations.

duration.tooltip: Duration of the output video in seconds (4-30).

generate_audio.tooltip: Enable audio generation for the output video.

output_format.tooltip: Container format of the output video.

prompt.tooltip: Text prompt for video generation. Put spoken lines in double quotes to steer the generated dialogue.

ratio.tooltip: Aspect ratio of the output video.

task_type.tooltip: What to do with the reference media. Every value except auto is validated when the task is submitted, so mismatched settings fail before generation starts. auto: the model infers the task from the prompt and inputs, and settings that conflict with its reading fail only after generation has started. reference: generate a new video guided by the reference images, videos, and audio. edit: change a connected reference video (add, remove, replace); the output keeps the source clip's own length and aspect ratio, and the duration and ratio widgets are ignored. extend: continue a connected reference video forward or backward; the prompt should say 'extend forward', 'extend backward', or 'continue', the aspect ratio follows the source clip, and the output contains only the newly generated segment of the duration you set, not the source clip.

ByteDanceSeedAudio.description: Generate speech, music, sound effects and multi-speaker dialogue from a single prompt with ByteDance Seed Audio 1.0. Describe the voice(s), emotion, ambience, background music and sound effects in the prompt, and include the lines to speak. Optionally pick a built-in preset voice, clone voices from up to 3 reference clips (tagged @Audio1-3 in the prompt), or derive a voice from a character image. Up to 2 minutes of audio per run. The multilingual model supports 20 languages and timestamp-based timing control.

model.tooltip: seed-audio-1.0-multilingual: 20 languages (English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Mexican & Castilian Spanish, Indonesian, German, Brazilian Portuguese, French, Thai, Vietnamese, Malay, Filipino, Italian, Russian, Dutch, Polish, Turkish, Swedish) plus per-sentence timing control via "[5.5s:8.0s] ..." timestamps. seed-audio-1.0: English and Chinese only, no timing control.

reference_audio_1.tooltip: Reference clip for voice cloning, tagged @Audio1 in the prompt. Up to 30s.

reference_audio_2.tooltip: Reference clip tagged @Audio2 in the prompt. Up to 30s.

reference_audio_3.tooltip: Reference clip tagged @Audio3 in the prompt. Up to 30s.

reference_image.tooltip: A single character image; the model derives a voice from it. Cannot be combined with reference audio.

preset_voice.tooltip: A built-in TTS 2.0 voice that reads the prompt. No reference clip needed, and @AudioN tags are not used in this mode.

reference_mode.tooltip: How to condition the voice: 'text only' (describe everything in the prompt), 'audio reference' (clone up to 3 voices, tagged @Audio1-3), 'image reference' (derive a voice from one character image), or 'preset voice' (pick a built-in named voice that reads the prompt).

seed.tooltip: Seed controls whether the node should re-run; results are non-deterministic regardless of seed.

text_prompt.tooltip: Describe the voice(s), emotion, pacing, ambience, background music and sound effects, and include the lines to speak (name characters inline for dialogue). In 'audio reference' mode, refer to connected clips by order as @Audio1, @Audio2, @Audio3. With the multilingual model, a quoted line can start with a timestamp range that controls when and how long it is spoken, e.g. "[5.5s:8.0s] Wait for me!". Write the prompt in the same language as the lines to speak. Maximum 3000 characters.

ByteDanceSeedAudio.name: ByteDanceSeedAudio

ByteDanceSeedreamLayerSeparationNode.description: Decompose an image into a background plate plus up to 16 repositionable transparent layers, each with stacking order, bounding box, name and description.

crop_layers.tooltip: Geometry of the layers/masks batch outputs (layer_stack is unaffected and always tight). Full canvas: each layer on a base-sized canvas at its bounding-box position - recompose directly with ImageCompositeMasked. Minimal size: each layer cropped to its bounding box (padded to the largest layer for batching) - much smaller tensors; rebuild placement with Layers From Bounding Boxes using the bboxes output.

size.tooltip: Output resolution level. 'auto' follows the input image size (clamped to the 1K-2K range).

ByteDanceVideoEnhanceNode.description: Upscales and restores a video with ByteDance vCube: super-resolution up to 8K, compression artifact and noise removal, colour and sharpness enhancement, optional frame interpolation.

bitrate_level.tooltip: Target bitrate of the delivered file, scaled to the output resolution and frame rate.

fps.tooltip: Output frame rate. A higher rate than the source enables AI frame interpolation; a lower one drops frames. 'source' keeps the source rate, up to 120 fps. Rates above 30 fps cost 2x, above 60 fps 4x.

short_side.tooltip: Short side of the output in pixels; the long side follows the source aspect ratio.

resolution.tooltip: Output resolution. The short side is set to the chosen level and the long side follows the source aspect ratio. 'source' keeps the source size, 'custom' sets the short side in pixels. Sources wider or taller than about 2.2:1 are billed one resolution tier higher.

enhance_style.tooltip: 'hd' applies a sharper enhancement; 'natural' reduces the strength for a softer, less sharpened look.

scene.tooltip: Preset tuned to the content: 'aigc' for AI-generated footage, 'common' for general video, 'ugc' for compressed phone clips, 'short_series' for drama with faces, 'old_film' for scratched or flickering archive footage.

enhance_style.tooltip: 'hd' applies a sharper enhancement; 'natural' reduces the strength for a softer, less sharpened look.

tool_version.tooltip: 'standard' balances speed and quality with 10+ enhancement algorithms. 'professional' uses 30+ algorithms for cinema-grade restoration, takes about 3x longer and costs 10x more.

video.tooltip: Video to enhance. The source resolution must be at most 2560x1440 (2K); the output size is set by the resolution input.

DA3GeometryToMesh.description: Convert a depth map into a triangulated 3D mesh.

batch_index.tooltip: Which image of a batch to convert. Per-image vertex counts differ so batches cannot be stacked.

confidence_threshold.tooltip: Exclude pixels whose per-image normalised confidence is below this value (0 = keep all, 1 = keep only the single most confident pixel). Used when the geometry has a confidence map (Small/Base models).

decimation.tooltip: Vertex stride. 1 = full resolution, 2 = half, etc.

discontinuity_threshold.tooltip: Drop triangles whose 3x3 depth span exceeds this fraction. 0 = off.

texture.tooltip: Use the source image as a base color texture.

use_sky_mask.tooltip: Exclude sky-probability pixels (sky >= 0.5) from the mesh. Used when the geometry has a sky map (Mono/Metric models).

DA3GeometryToMesh.name: DA3GeometryToMesh

DA3Inference.description: Run Depth Anything 3 on an image. In multi-view mode each image is treated as a separate view of the same scene.

pose_method.tooltip:
How the camera field-of-view is estimated (for Small/Base models only).
- cam_dec: learned from image features.
- ray_pose: derived geometrically from the model's 3D ray output.
Affects perspective correctness of the 3D output. Try both if results look distorted.

ref_view_strategy.tooltip:
Which view acts as the geometric anchor.
- saddle_balanced: the view most 'average' across all others (best general choice).
- saddle_sim_range: the view most visually distinct from the others.
- first / middle: fixed positional picks.

mode.tooltip:
mono: single view image (works with any model variant).
multiview: all images processed together for geometric consistency + camera pose (for Small/Base models only).

resize_method.tooltip:
upper_bound_resize: scale so the longest side = resolution (caps memory, default).
lower_bound_resize: scale so the shortest side = resolution (preserves more detail on tall/wide images, uses more memory).

resolution.tooltip:
Resolution the model runs at (longest side, multiple of 14).
Lower = faster / less VRAM.
Higher = more detail.
Output is upsampled back to the original size.

DA3Inference.name: DA3Inference

DA3Render.description: Render a depth map, confidence map, or sky mask from Depth Anything 3 geometry data.

apply_sky_clip.tooltip: Clip sky-region depth to the 99th percentile of foreground depth before normalisation. Requires a sky key in the da3_geometry input (for Mono/Metric models only).

normalization.tooltip:
- v2_style: mean/std normalisation for perceptually balanced results (default).
- min_max: stretches the full depth range to [0, 1] for maximum contrast.
- raw: no scaling,preserves metric units for Metric model.

DecimateMesh.description: Simplifies a mesh to a target face count using QEM, on the active compute device. 'midpoint' is the cumesh-faithful preset (best quality, preserves thin features / hair); 'qem' places vertices at the QEM optimum with line/feature-edge controls. Output stays welded.

clamp_v_to_edge.tooltip: Project the QEM-optimal position onto the collapsed edge segment.

feature_edge_min_dihedral_deg.tooltip: Minimum dihedral angle (degree) to count an edge as a feature edge.

feature_edge_quadric_weight.tooltip: Extra quadric weight on dihedral feature edges (creases). 0 = off.

line_quadric_weight.tooltip: Per-edge line-quadric weight; preserves sharp ridges/valleys. 0 = off.

DecimateMesh.name: DecimateMesh

system_prompt.default:
You are an expert image-generation engine. You must ALWAYS produce an image.
Interpret all user input—regardless of format, intent, or abstraction—as literal visual directives for image composition.
If a prompt is conversational or lacks specific visual details, you must creatively invent a concrete visual scenario that depicts the concept.
Prioritize generating the visual representation above any text, formatting, or conversational requests.

response_modalities.tooltip: Choose 'IMAGE' for image-only output, or 'IMAGE+TEXT' to return both the generated image and a text response.

seed.tooltip: When the seed is fixed to a specific value, the model makes a best effort to provide the same response for repeated requests. Deterministic output isn't guaranteed. Also, changing the model or parameter settings, such as the temperature, can cause variations in the response even when you use the same seed value. By default, a random seed value is used.

files.tooltip: Optional file(s) to use as context for the model. Accepts inputs from the Gemini Input Files node.

audio.tooltip: Optional audio clip to use as context for the model.

images.tooltip: Optional image(s) to use as context for the model. Up to 16 images.

max_output_tokens.tooltip: Maximum tokens to generate, including the model's internal thinking. With thinking_level HIGH, a low value can leave no room for the answer; raise this if responses come back empty or truncated. The model stops early when finished, so a higher cap costs nothing extra for short replies.

prompt.tooltip: Text input to the model. Include detailed instructions, questions, or context.

seed.tooltip: Seed for sampling. Set to 0 for a random seed. Deterministic output isn't guaranteed.

system_prompt.tooltip: Foundational instructions that dictate the model's behavior.

thinking_level.tooltip: How hard the model reasons internally before answering. HIGH improves quality on difficult tasks but costs more (thinking) tokens and is slower.

video.tooltip: Optional video clip to use as context for the model.

video_processing.tooltip: How the model reads the attached video. `static` samples frames at a fixed rate and sends all of them as context; `agentic` lets the model navigate the timeline itself and load only the frames, audio or transcript it needs, which costs far fewer input tokens on long videos.

GeminiVideoOmni.description: Generate a video with audio from a text prompt using Google's Gemini Omni Flash model. Optionally provide reference images and/or videos to guide or edit the result. Describe the desired length (3-10s) and aspect ratio (16:9 or 9:16) directly in the prompt.

images.tooltip: Optional reference image(s) to guide or animate the video. Up to 14 images.

prompt.tooltip: Describe the video to generate. Specify the length and aspect ratio directly in the prompt, e.g. "a 6-second clip in 16:9". Length may be 3-10 seconds; the aspect ratio must be 16:9 (landscape) or 9:16 (portrait). The output is 720p, 24 FPS, with audio.

temperature.tooltip: Controls randomness. Lower is more focused/deterministic, higher is more varied.

top_p.tooltip: Nucleus sampling: sample from the smallest token set whose cumulative probability reaches top_p.

videos.tooltip: Optional reference video(s) to guide or edit. Up to 3 videos, each up to 10 seconds long.

model.tooltip: The Gemini video model used to generate the video.

seed.tooltip: Seed controls whether the node should re-run; results are non-deterministic regardless of seed.

GeminiVideoOmni.name: GeminiVideoOmni

GeminiVideoOmniV2.description: Generate a video with audio from a text prompt using Google's Gemini Omni Flash models. Optionally provide reference images and/or videos to guide or edit the result. Describe the desired length (3-10s) directly in the prompt.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: Output aspect ratio: 16:9 (landscape) or 9:16 (portrait). The 'edit' and 'extend' tasks keep the aspect ratio of the input video instead.

images.tooltip: Optional reference image(s) to guide or animate the video. Up to 14 images; with the 'image_to_video' task the first one is the starting frame and an optional second one is the ending frame.

prompt.tooltip: Describe the video to generate, or the edit to apply to an attached video. Specify the length directly in the prompt, e.g. "a 6-second clip" or, for the 'extend' task, "extend by 5 seconds"; the generated length may be 3-10 seconds and defaults to 10. The output has audio.

seed.tooltip: Seed controls whether the node should re-run; results are non-deterministic regardless of seed.

task_type.tooltip: What to do with the prompt and the attached media. With 'auto' the model decides. 'text_to_video' generates from the prompt alone and rejects attached media. 'image_to_video' animates one image, or interpolates from a starting frame to an ending frame when two are attached. 'reference_to_video' treats the attached media as subject references. 'edit' rewrites exactly one attached video, and 'extend' appends new footage to it, so the output starts with the input video.

videos.tooltip: Optional reference video(s) to guide or edit. Up to 3 videos, each up to 10 seconds long.

HiDreamO1PatchSeamSmoothing.description: Average the model output across multiple shifted patch-grid positions during the late portion of sampling. Cancels seams.

blend.tooltip: average: equal-weight mean. window: Hann-windowed weighting favoring each pass away from its patch boundaries. median: per-pixel median, rejects wraparound-outlier passes.

end_percent.tooltip: Sampling progress at which the blend turns OFF.

passes.tooltip: Number of passes per gated step. 2/4 = fixed. ramp_*: pass count increases as sampling approaches end (more smoothing where seams are most visible).

pattern.tooltip: Shift layout. single_shift: one pass at the natural patch grid + others offset. symmetric: all passes off-grid, shifts split around origin.

start_percent.tooltip: Sampling progress (0=start, 1=end) at which the blend turns ON.

strength.tooltip: Interpolation between the natural-grid pred (0) and the averaged result (1).

HiDreamO1PatchSeamSmoothing.name: HiDreamO1PatchSeamSmoothing

seed.tooltip: Seed for reproducible generation. With prompt_upsampling OFF, the same seed and settings return the same image; with ON/AUTO the prompt rewrite varies per run — reproduce a result by reusing its final_prompt output with prompt_upsampling OFF and the same seed.

quality.tooltip: Speed/price/quality tier. MEDIUM is the everyday default; HIGH for complex prompts, fine detail and difficult text; VERY_LOW/LOW for drafts at scale. Difficult text renders poorly below MEDIUM.

resolution.tooltip: Output size class (exact pixels follow the aspect ratio, e.g. 16:9 gives 1280x720 at 1K and 2560x1440 at 2K). Prefer HIGH + 2K for crisp typography.

ImageColorSpace.description: Convert sRGB, linear Rec.709, HDR (Rec.2020 HLG), and HDR PQ (Rec.2020 PQ). Linear 1.0 uses the same 203-nit reference white as sRGB; HLG uses a 1000-nit reference display. Linear output and linear-to-HDR conversions preserve extended values without tone mapping. SDR output and PQ-to-HLG conversion tone-map excess luminance across the batch and compress out-of-gamut colors. Conversions compute in float32 and return the intermediate device and dtype. Straight alpha is not color-transformed.

destination.tooltip: Color space of the output pixels. Set the save node to this same color space.

source.tooltip: Color space of the input pixels.

ImageColorSpace.name: ImageColorSpace

compositor.tooltip: Layered composition saved by the compositor editor.

layers.tooltip: Layer stack to composite; build it with Add Layer. Items are stacked by z_index, batch frames inside an item expand to consecutive layers, and item placement, opacity, and blend mode define the initial composition. Without an explicit document canvas the size is a best-effort maximum extent of the placed layers. A saved composition that matches the current inputs takes priority.

background.tooltip: Background color behind the masked subject.

grow_mask.tooltip: Grow or shrink the mask by this many pixels before cropping.

height.tooltip: Output height in pixels.

pad_factor.tooltip: Extra margin around the mask bounding box as a multiplier.

width.tooltip: Output width in pixels.

LTXVAddGeneratedKeyframes.description: Append detailing keyframes to a video latent. Each keyframe is one latent frame of tokens whose RoPE position spans a single pixel frame; they are denoised with the video and are not part of the decoded output. Placement is one slot every interval_frames pixels, skipping I2V frames, existing guides, and detailing keyframes already on the cond. Connected keyframes are content only and are re-placed on this canvas unless frame_indices is set. Pull them back out with LTXV Separate Generated Keyframes. Requires a checkpoint trained for generated keyframes (one carrying keyframes_abs_pos_embedding).

frame_indices.tooltip: Optional pixel-frame indices. Leave empty to place from interval_frames on the current canvas. When set, this list is the placement (connected keyframes are matched in order). The last frame is allowed; frame 0 is not (it is already a standalone token).

interval_frames.tooltip: Pixel-frame stride for auto placement. Default 24 is about one keyframe per second at 24 fps. Occupied pixels are skipped. Ignored when frame_indices is set.

keyframes.tooltip: Optional content to initialize the new keyframes with. Connect keyframes from an earlier Separate (same spatial size), or a plain video latent to copy the nearest frame at each new slot (e.g. after temporal upscale). These are still denoised, not pinned as guides. Recorded indices on a keyframes latent are ignored unless frame_indices is set. Only has an effect when sampling starts below sigma 1.

latent.tooltip: Plain 5D video latent to generate keyframes alongside. Add them before Concat AV Latent.

negative.tooltip: Negative conditioning the keyframes are attached to.

positive.tooltip: Positive conditioning the keyframes are attached to.

vae.tooltip: Only used to read the latent scale factors.

LTXVAddGeneratedKeyframes.name: LTXVAddGeneratedKeyframes

attention_mask.tooltip: Optional pixel-space spatial mask. Controls per-region conditioning influence via self-attention, multiplied by strength.

iclora_parameters.tooltip: Optional IC-LoRA parameters from a Get IC-LoRA Parameters node. Used for adjusting guide processing as required by certain IC-LoRAs (eg. those with a reference_downscale_factor > 1). When chained, each LTXVAddGuide uses only the parameters connected to it.

frame_idx.tooltip: Frame index to start the conditioning at. For single-frame images or videos with 1-8 frames, any frame_idx value is acceptable. For videos with 9+ frames, frame_idx must be divisible by 8, otherwise it will be rounded down to the nearest multiple of 8. Negative values are counted from the end of the video.

image.tooltip: Image or video to condition the latent video on. Must be 8*n + 1 frames. If the video is not 8*n + 1 frames, it will be cropped to the nearest 8*n + 1 frames.

LTXVAddLatentGuide.description: Pins an already-encoded latent as a guide, for when the guide comes out of an earlier stage rather than an image. Same effect as LTXV Add Guide without the VAE decode/encode round trip. A guide that is spatially smaller than the target (an IC-LoRA or detailing reference) is dilated onto a sparse grid, and its RoPE end positions are expanded by the same ratio so it covers the target canvas instead of addressing only the top-left corner of it.

attention_mask.tooltip: Optional pixel-space spatial mask. Controls per-region conditioning influence via self-attention, multiplied by strength.

guiding_latent.tooltip: Guide latent. Its spatial size must divide the target's by the same whole number on both axes; equal size pins it as-is, half size is treated as an x2 IC-LoRA reference.

latent.tooltip: Target video latent the guide is pinned onto.

latent_idx.tooltip: Latent frame index to start the guide at, counted in latent frames rather than pixel frames. Negative values place the guide on frames before the start of the latent, not counted back from its end.

strength.tooltip: Capped at 1.0. A dilated guide marks its padding positions with a negative denoise mask so the model drops them; above 1.0 the kept positions would go negative too and the whole guide would be dropped. Amplify beyond 1.0 with attention_mask instead.

LTXVAddLatentGuide.name: LTXVAddLatentGuide

context_schedule.tooltip: Step-dependent scheduling algorithm for context windows.

context_stride.tooltip: The stride of the context window; only applicable to uniform schedules.

freenoise.tooltip: Whether to apply FreeNoise noise shuffling, improves window blending.

fuse_method.tooltip: The method to use to fuse the context windows.

retain_first_frame.tooltip: Retain the first latent frame in every context window (may help retain initial reference).

split_conds_to_windows.tooltip: Whether to split multiple conditionings (created by ConditionCombine) to each window based on region index.

LTXVDurationPredictor.description: Predicts the natural shot duration for a prompt using the LTX 2.4 duration head (loaded with ModelPatchLoader), and snaps it to the VAE's 8k+1 frame grid.

LTXVDurationPredictor.name: LTXVDurationPredictor

audio_vae.tooltip: The Audio VAE model to get configuration from.

batch_size.tooltip: The number of latent audio samples in the batch.

LTXVFreezeLatent.description: Set noise_mask to 0 so this latent is kept clean during sampling. Works on video or audio. Typical uses: freeze audio before Concat AV so it only provides cross-attention, or freeze any latent that should not be denoised.

latent.tooltip: Video or audio latent to freeze. Audio is 4D; video is 5D.

LTXVFreezeLatent.name: LTXVFreezeLatent

LTXVGeneratedKeyframesToGuides.description: Pin generated keyframes from an earlier stage as frozen image guides on a later canvas. They are decoded as standalone frames, resized if needed, and written with noise_mask=0 so they are not denoised again. After a temporal upscale, recorded indices are scaled from the canvas they were generated on onto this one (same moments). Use override_frame_indices to set positions explicitly. To keep generating (and denoising) keyframes at new positions, use Add Generated Keyframes instead.

override_frame_indices.tooltip: Optional — pin at these pixel frames instead of the recorded (or auto-scaled) positions. Provide one index per keyframe. Leave empty to reuse recorded positions, or to scale them when the target canvas is a different length (e.g. after temporal x2).

keyframes.tooltip: The keyframes output of LTXV Separate Generated Keyframes, which carries the pixel frame index each keyframe was generated at.

latent.tooltip: The target video latent to add the guides to, e.g. the temporally upscaled one.

strength.tooltip: Guide strength. 1.0 is a hard pin; lower values relax it.

LTXVGeneratedKeyframesToGuides.name: LTXVGeneratedKeyframesToGuides

LTXVModalityGuidance.description: Cross-modal (audio-video) guidance for LTXV-AV. Runs one extra forward pass per step with the a2v/v2a cross-attention severed, then pushes the result toward the coupled prediction - strengthening audio-visual sync (e.g. lip-sync). Reference default modality_scale is 3.0. Stacks with the dual-CFG guider and STG. Set to 1.0 to disable (no extra pass).
LTXVModalityGuidance.name: LTXVModalityGuidance

img_compression.tooltip: Amount of compression to apply on image.

LTXVReferenceAudio.description: Set reference audio for ID-LoRA speaker identity transfer. Encodes a reference audio clip into the conditioning and optionally patches the model with identity guidance (extra forward pass without reference, amplifying the speaker identity effect).

end_percent.tooltip: End of the sigma range where identity guidance is active.

identity_guidance_scale.tooltip: Strength of identity guidance. Runs an extra forward pass without reference each step to amplify speaker identity. Set to 0 to disable (no extra pass).

reference_audio.tooltip: Reference audio clip whose speaker identity to transfer. ~5 seconds recommended (training duration). Shorter or longer clips may degrade voice identity transfer.

start_percent.tooltip: Start of the sigma range where identity guidance is active.

LTXVReferenceAudio.name: LTXVReferenceAudio

stretch.tooltip: Stretch the sigmas to be in the range [terminal, 1].

terminal.tooltip: The terminal value of the sigmas after stretching.

LTXVSeparateAVLatent.description: Split a joint AV latent into its video and audio latents (any AV model, e.g. LTXV or MiniMax H3).
LTXVSeparateAVLatent.name: LTXVSeparateAVLatent

LTXVSeparateGeneratedKeyframes.description: Split the generated keyframes added by LTXV Add Generated Keyframes back out of a sampled latent, and remove them from the conditioning. Separate them before spatially upscaling the video latent. Do not run LTXV Crop Guides first — it treats generated keyframes as disposable guides and drops them.

keyframes_to_batch.tooltip: Return the keyframes as a batch of single-frame latents. Leave off to get them as one multi-frame latent, which is what the latent upsampler and a later Add Generated Keyframes expect.

LTXVSeparateGeneratedKeyframes.name: LTXVSeparateGeneratedKeyframes

LTXVSpatioTemporalGuidance.description: Runs one extra pass per step with the self-attention of the selected blocks degraded to a value-passthrough, then guides away from it - improving spatial detail and motion coherence.

blocks.tooltip: Comma-separated transformer block indices to perturb.

LTXVSpatioTemporalGuidance.name: LTXVSpatioTemporalGuidance

LayersFromBoundingBoxes.description: Turn an image batch plus its bounding boxes into a layer stack, one layer per frame, each placed by its own box. Use this when a node emits layers as a batch - a batch carries a single placement for every frame, so the individual positions are otherwise lost.

canvas_height.tooltip: Document canvas height. 0 derives it from the placed layers.

canvas_width.tooltip: Document canvas width. 0 derives it from the placed layers.

crop_to_content.tooltip: Crop each frame to metadata.content_rect where present and place the content at the box position plus the rect offset. Leave on for batches whose frames are padded - it keeps only the real content at its true spot.

layers.tooltip: Layer stack to append to. Leave unconnected to start a new stack.

mask.tooltip: Per-frame transparency, index-aligned with the image batch (1 = transparent, LoadImage convention).

bboxes.tooltip: Placement boxes, index-aligned with the image batch. Accepts bounding boxes (x, y, width, height), normalized elements (with a 'bbox' - these need canvas_width/canvas_height to resolve to pixels), or a JSON string of either. Frames without a matching box are placed at the origin. A box's width/height scales the layer to fit it. metadata.name (or desc) and metadata.z_index are used when present, and metadata.content_rect (frame-relative) crops the frame to its real content.

image.tooltip: Image batch; each frame becomes one layer.

LayersFromBoundingBoxes.name: LayersFromBoundingBoxes

PrunaImageToVideoNode.description: Animates an image into a video using Pruna video models, with an optional last frame, generated sound or audio track.

audio.tooltip: Audio that drives the motion and becomes the soundtrack. At least 1 second long; audio longer than 20 seconds is truncated. Sets the video length instead of duration.

last_frame.tooltip: Image the video ends on. Its aspect ratio must be close to the first frame's.

draft.tooltip: Faster, less detailed render, billed at 60% of the standard rate.

duration.tooltip: Length of the video in seconds. 'auto' lets the model choose the length from the prompt. Ignored when audio is connected: the video then follows the audio length, rounded up to a whole second, up to 20 seconds.

first_frame.tooltip: Image the video starts from. The output keeps the aspect ratio of this image.

fps.tooltip: Frames per second. 48 fps is not available with draft at 1080p.

generate_audio.tooltip: Generate a soundtrack for the video. Ignored when audio is connected, which becomes the soundtrack instead.

prompt.tooltip: Describes how the scene moves and sounds. Up to 5000 characters.

resolution.tooltip: Output resolution. 720p renders about 0.9 megapixels (1280x704 at 16:9), 1080p about 2 megapixels (1920x1088 at 16:9).

seed.tooltip: Seed for the generation. The same seed reproduces a result exactly only when enhance_prompt is off.

model.tooltip: Model to use.

RemeshMesh.description: Re-extracts a uniformly tessellated mesh via a narrow-band distance field + Dual Contouring, on the active compute device. Normalizes messy / non-manifold / self-intersecting topology; run before Decimate Mesh to hit an exact face count. Output stays welded.

band.tooltip: Narrow-band width in voxel units. In UDF mode also offsets the surface.

drop_small_components.tooltip: Drop components below this fraction of the largest's face count. 0 disables.

fix_poles.tooltip: Collapse valence-3 vertex pairs (DC T-junction artifact).

precluster_max_verts.tooltip: Cap input vertex count before the field queries, inputs above this are cluster-decimated to it first. Prevents OOM on huge meshes.

project_back.tooltip: Linearly interpolate vertices toward the original surface (0 = pure DC, 1 = snapped).

resolution.tooltip: Voxel grid resolution (output density). 256 ~ 100k faces, 512 ~ 1M. For an exact face count, follow with Decimate Mesh.

drop_enclosed_components.tooltip: Drop components inside the largest's bbox that fail a point-in-mesh raycast. Disable for legitimate nested parts.

drop_inverted_components.tooltip: Drop inward-normal (negative-volume) closed components — the UDF inner shell.

qef.tooltip: QEF (Quadratic Error Function) dual-vertex placement for sharper edges.

manifold.tooltip: Manifold Dual Contouring: 1-4 dual verts/voxel for multi-sheet cases. Slower.

RenderSplat.description: Render a gaussian splat as an image with an anisotropic EWA rasterizer (oriented elliptical splats, antialiased, depth-sorted front-to-back). The camera comes from a camera_info input (Load / Preview 3D, or a Create Camera Info node); leave it empty to auto-frame the splat. Set frames greater than 1 for a turntable batch of images to feed a Video node.

bg_image.tooltip: Optional background plate composited behind the splat (overrides the solid background colour). Resized to the render size; a batch is used per frame, a single image for all. color/clay only.

frames.tooltip: -1, 0, 1 = single still image; >1 = turntable, the camera orbits over a full 360 turn (works with any camera_info). Negative value orbits the other way.

headlight_shading.tooltip: Diffuse shading from a light at the camera (headlight), using the splat surfel normals: darkens surfaces that turn away from view to reveal form/curvature. 0 = flat albedo, 1 = strongest shading.

opacity_threshold.tooltip: Cull gaussians with opacity below this (removes faint floaters).

render_style.tooltip: What the image output shows: color, clay (neutral-albedo shaded), depth (near=bright), normal (OpenGL normal map).

sharpen.tooltip: Sharpen overlapping splats: 1.0 = physically-correct blend; higher biases each pixel toward its dominant (nearest) splat for crisper texture, without shrinking splats or opening gaps. Non-physical above 1.

splat_scale.tooltip: Multiplier on each splat's projected footprint (lower = crisper points, higher = softer/fuller surface).

brow_strength.tooltip: Multiplier on brow/cheek/sneer shapes. MediaPipe outputs ~0.1-0.3; 2-3x.

eye_strength.tooltip: Multiplier on eye shapes. MediaPipe rarely exceeds 0.5; 2-3x often needed.

input_threshold.tooltip: Deadzone on MediaPipe's raw output (below = zero, above = linear remap).

mouth_strength.tooltip: Multiplier on mouth/jaw shapes. MediaPipe's jawOpen saturates near 1.0.

strength.tooltip: Global multiplier on all blendshapes. >1 exaggerates.

Colorspace of the input tensor. The EXR is always written as scene-linear in the matching gamut.
sRGB — input is sRGB-encoded Rec.709; the inverse sRGB EOTF is applied.
HDR — input is HLG-encoded Rec.2020 (BT.2100); the inverse HLG OETF is applied to get scene-linear light.
linear — input is already scene-linear (Rec.709 primaries); written through unchanged. Use this for renderer/compositor output.

SelectCLIPDevice.description:
Place the CLIP text encoder on a specific device (default / cpu / gpu:N).

- "default" restores the device assigned by the loader.
- "cpu" pins both the load and offload device to CPU.
- "gpu:N" pins the load device to the Nth available GPU.

When the selected device does not exist on the current machine
(e.g. a workflow built on a 2-GPU box opened on a 1-GPU box),
the node passes the CLIP through unchanged and logs a message
instead of failing.
SelectCLIPDevice.name: SelectCLIPDevice

SelectModelDevice.description:
Place the diffusion model on a specific device (default / cpu / gpu:N).

- "default" restores the device assigned by the loader (even after a
  prior Select Model Device call).
- "cpu" pins both the load and offload device to CPU.
- "gpu:N" pins the load device to the Nth available GPU; the offload
  device is restored to the loader's original choice.

When the requested device differs from the device the input model is
already on, a fresh model is spawned via the loader's reload factory
(cached_patcher_init) so the new patcher owns independent weights on
the new device. Loaders that don't support multigpu (no factory) will
cause the node to pass through unchanged with a warning.

If the workflow already has MultiGPU CFG Split applied and the chosen
GPU collides with one of the existing multigpu clones, that clone is
dropped so two patchers don't end up bound to the same device.

When the selected device does not exist on the current machine
(e.g. a workflow built on a 2-GPU box opened on a 1-GPU box),
the node passes the model through unchanged and logs a message
instead of failing.

NOTE: Placing Select Model Device *after* a node that has already
consumed the same model (e.g. a KSampler that ran on this model on
the original device) is not recommended -- any state the prior
consumer mutated on the original model will be observed when the
selected device matches the original (fast path). Place Select Model
Device before any consumer of the model.
SelectModelDevice.name: SelectModelDevice

SelectVAEDevice.description:
Place the VAE on a specific device (default / gpu:N).

- "default" restores the device assigned by the loader.
- "gpu:N" pins the load device to the Nth available GPU; the offload
  device is set to the standard VAE offload device.

CPU is intentionally not exposed in the UI for the VAE; if a workflow
supplies "cpu" anyway (e.g. opened from another machine), the request
is dropped with a log message and the VAE is passed through unchanged.

When the selected device does not exist on the current machine
(e.g. a workflow built on a 2-GPU box opened on a 1-GPU box),
the node passes the VAE through unchanged and logs a message
instead of failing.
SelectVAEDevice.name: SelectVAEDevice

SplatToMesh.description: Extract a coloured mesh from a gaussian splat.

color_sharpen.tooltip: Crisp up the vertex texture: 1.0 = physically-correct blend; higher biases each voxel's colour toward its dominant gaussian instead of averaging neighbours (de-smears the texture). Colour only - geometry is unchanged.

kernel.tooltip: Max splat half-width in voxels. Each gaussian is rasterized over a window sized to its own 3-sigma, capped here - small surfels stay cheap, large ones aren't truncated. Raise if sparse splats leave gaps.

level.tooltip: Iso-surface level. Auto-picked by Otsu; this biases it (1.0 = auto, lower = fatter/more-connected surface, higher = thinner/tighter).

min_component.tooltip: Drop connected components smaller than this many vertices (0 = keep all). Removes detached floater blobs and the inner shell of the double wall.

min_opacity.tooltip: Ignore gaussians fainter than this before meshing.

resolution.tooltip: Density-grid resolution along the longest axis. Higher = finer surface, more VRAM/time (grows with resolution^3).

smooth.tooltip: Taubin mesh-smoothing iterations. Smooths the surface without shrinking it (volume-preserving), unlike blurring the density. 0 = raw surface.

WanAnimate2Cache.description: Caches the pose-video's per-block activations so it runs once instead of on every sampling step. Roughly halves generation time Tradeoff is ~12.5 GB of system RAM at 480x832/81 frames in bf16 (scales with resolution and length). With context windows each window is cached separately, so RAM scales with the window count; use the static_standard schedule, as uniform schedules shift the windows every step and nothing ever recurs to hit the cache.

device.tooltip: Where to keep the cache. cpu (RAM) is the safe choice, the cache will not fit in VRAM alongside the model at typical sizes. gpu (VRAM) can be faster if it fits.

dtype.tooltip: Storage precision. default stores the activations in the model's compute dtype. int8 halves the cache, int4 quarters it, convrot is used to retain accuracy.

WanAnimate2Cache.name: WanAnimate2Cache

clip_vision_output.tooltip: CLIP vision of the reference image.

clip_vision_output_pose.tooltip: CLIP vision of the pose video's first frame. Defaults to clip_vision_output.

continue_motion.tooltip: Previous motion sequence to continue from for temporal consistency.

pose_video.tooltip: The video whose motion is transferred to the reference character.

positive_pose.tooltip: Prompt for the pose-video branch, describing the motion rather than the character. Defaults to positive. Used for both the cond and uncond passes.

batch_size.tooltip: Number of videos to generate simultaneously.

height.tooltip: Output video height in pixels.

pose_end_percent.tooltip: Sampling percent at which the pose influence ends. Motion is mostly established early, so e.g. 0.7 can loosen fine detail while keeping the choreography.

pose_start_percent.tooltip: Sampling percent at which the pose influence starts. Outside the window the pose branch is skipped entirely, which also speeds those steps up.

pose_strength.tooltip: Scales the pose video's influence on the motion. 1.0 is the trained behavior; below weakens adherence, above amplifies. 0.0 mutes it but does not fully remove it.

reference_image_strength.tooltip: Scales how strongly generated frames attend to the reference image's latent frame. Below 1.0 loosens identity/appearance adherence (e.g. to let the prompt restyle), above tightens it against drift.

video_frame_offset.tooltip: Frames to seek into the pose video. Connect to the video_frame_offset output of the previous node when extending.

width.tooltip: Output video width in pixels.
